conclusion: No specific blocker found within the declared source-relative case-assignment theorem and bounded transport.
checked: The inductive Reference relation is not defined by recognize output. It requires ledger membership, proper-name/singular/triptote subject, adjective/singular/triptote predicate, exact rendering and independently checked literal nasb/raf endings.

recognize enumerates the full finite ledger product and filters by direct field/byte conditions. The iff theorem uses explicit component equivalences; source equality is equality of the complete rendered byte list.
CaseTagAllows permits the required tag or unknown but never replaces WrittenNasb/WrittenRaf. The transport additionally rejects known tags contrary to observed tanwin.

pending retains only pairs consistent with the stated possible-field/ending profile; pending blocks completeWithinFragment. This is not a theorem that the input ledger enumerates every Arabic reading.

Transport uses source_hex as input, validates canonical lowercase byte pairs and UTF-8, rejects duplicate reading IDs, enforces bounded request/ledger/output sizes, and reports invalid/resource failures separately from linguistic rejection.
No custom axiom, sorry, admit, native_decide or unsafe proof bypass was observed in either reviewed file.
explicit_limits: SurfaceWithin is a byte-boundary predicate, not an Arabic-word classifier: with a caller-asserted lexical category it can admit non-Arabic/control/punctuation bytes outside its small forbidden list. This is consistent with the documented conditional premise, and must not be reported as ordinary Arabic membership.

The theorem establishes case assignments in this reference, not full adjectival agreement: it has no gender field. In particular, it does not certify grammaticality of every supplied name/adjective combination.

Interpreted category/number/declension/sense, witness authenticity, lexical exhaustiveness, reference identity and external truth are outside the theorem. Ledger source acquisition and the Python-to-Lean/JSON/OS refinement require their separate recorded evidence.

Only regular written accusative alif (either encoded tanwin position) and nominative/genitive tanwin are covered. Taa-marbuta, hamza exceptions, unmarked prose, punctuation and other nominal classes are not generalized.
